q: The three mandatory scheme-related documents are:
e: The three mandatory documents are Scheme Information Document (SID), Statement of Additional Information (SAI), and Key Information Memorandum (KIM).

q: The Scheme Information Document (SID) primarily contains:
e: SID contains scheme-specific details — investment objective, asset allocation, risks, fees, fund manager. SAI has statutory info about the AMC/Mutual Fund.

q: The Key Information Memorandum (KIM) is:
o: A summary of SID and SAI for investors
A standalone document not related to SID/SAI
Filed only with SEBI, not given to investors
e: KIM is a summary of SID and SAI. SEBI mandates that every application form must be accompanied by the KIM.

q: In the case of a fundamental attribute change, the AMC must:
o: Issue addendum and provide a 30-day no-load exit window
e: Fundamental attribute changes (Reg 18(15A)) require an addendum and a no-load exit option for at least 30 days.

q: Frequency of mandatory KIM updation:
e: KIM is updated at least once every half-year, within one month from the end of the half-year (Sept and March).

q: Riskometer must be evaluated and disclosed by the AMC:
e: The Riskometer is evaluated and updated on a monthly basis. Any change must be conveyed via notice-cum-addendum and SMS/email to unitholders.

q: The Riskometer of a scheme is published in the:
e: The Riskometer and the suitability statement appear on the front (cover) page of the SID.

q: Specialized Investment Funds (SIFs) use which risk indicator (instead of Riskometer)?
e: SIFs use a Risk-Band with 5 levels (Risk Band Level 1 lowest to Level 5 highest), as SIFs are inherently riskier than mutual fund schemes.

q: SEBI's role with respect to scheme-related documents is to:
e: SEBI does NOT approve or disapprove SID/SAI — it provides observations which the AMC must incorporate. The documents are "vetted" not "approved".

q: The "Caveat Emptor" principle in mutual fund investing means:
o: Buyer beware — investor presumed to have read scheme documents
e: Investors are presumed to have read and understood scheme documents before investing. They cannot later claim ignorance of disclosed facts.

q: Among the six Riskometer levels, "Moderately High" risk is depicted using which colour?
e: The 6 levels: Low (Irish Green), Low to Moderate (Chartreuse), Moderate (Neon Yellow), Moderately High (Caramel), High (Dark Orange), Very High (Red).

q: An interim change to a scheme document, before the next regular update, is effected through:
e: Interim changes are effected via an addendum, which becomes part of the scheme documents and must accompany KIM until the next update.

q: Riskometer evaluation is required to be done:
e: Riskometer must be evaluated and updated on a monthly basis. Changes must be communicated via notice-cum-addendum and SMS/email to unitholders.

q: For a Specialized Investment Fund (SIF), the risk indicator is the:
e: SIFs are riskier than mutual fund schemes; SEBI mandates a Risk-Band with 5 levels for SIFs to differentiate from the mutual fund Riskometer.

q: The KIM must be accompanied by:
e: SEBI mandates every application form to be accompanied by KIM. The KIM may also include the latest applicable addendum.

q: A scheme's SID has been "vetted" by SEBI. This means:
o: SEBI has provided observations the AMC must incorporate
e: Vetting = SEBI provides observations; AMC must incorporate. SEBI does not approve, certify or rank schemes.

q: "Please read the scheme related documents carefully" — these documents refer to:
o: SID and audited balance sheet of AMC
Scheme Information Document and Statement of Additional Information
e: The "scheme related documents" referenced in the standard mutual fund disclaimer are the SID and SAI.

q: SID and SAI are prepared in the format prescribed by:
o: AMFI as part of Code of Conduct
AMFI as part of Best Practices Circular
Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
e: SID and SAI must follow SEBI-prescribed format. Contents flow in the same sequence as in the prescribed format.

q: Which of the following is NOT a statutory document?
e: Fund factsheet is NOT a statutory document — though it is published monthly. SID, SAI and KIM are statutory.

q: As per fair valuation principles laid out by SEBI, it is mandatory to disclose the valuation policy in:
e: Valuation policy is disclosed in the Statement of Additional Information (SAI), as part of fair valuation principles mandated by SEBI.

q: For mutual fund schemes, an SID is initially valid for:
o: Until a "material change" occurs (with periodic updates within 6 months of FY half-end)
e: SID remains effective until a material change. Open-ended/Interval scheme SIDs are updated within 6 months of FY half-end (Sept and March data).

q: The offer document (SID) of a mutual fund scheme must disclose investor grievance history of the AMC for the past:
e: SID must disclose investor grievance history for the past 3 fiscal years — number of complaints received, redressed, pending.

q: Pending litigation or penalties levied on the sponsors or AMC must be disclosed in the:
e: Pending litigation, penalties, and material regulatory actions on sponsors/AMC/trustees MUST be disclosed in the SID and SAI for transparency.

q: A "Glossary of Defined Terms" in the offer document is:
e: A glossary of defined terms is mandatory in the offer document — defines all special terms and abbreviations used in the document for investor clarity.

q: The Due Diligence Certificate filed with SEBI by the AMC for an NFO confirms that:
o: The draft offer document complies with SEBI regulations and disclosures are true, fair and adequate
e: Due Diligence Certificate confirms regulatory compliance, completeness, and accuracy of disclosures. It does NOT guarantee performance — that is explicitly disclaimed.

q: The Due Diligence Certificate must be signed by:
o: The Compliance Officer of the AMC
e: The Compliance Officer of the AMC must sign the Due Diligence Certificate filed along with the draft offer document.

q: Standard risk factors (in scheme documents) are:
o: Common to all mutual fund schemes (as prescribed by SEBI)
e: Standard risk factors are common to all schemes and prescribed by SEBI. Specific risk factors are unique to the particular scheme.

q: The Statement of Additional Information (SAI) updation cycle is:
o: Annually within 3 months of FY-end + material changes on ongoing basis
e: Regular SAI update: by end of 3 months from financial year-end. Material changes must be updated on an ongoing basis and uploaded to AMC and AMFI websites.

q: Monthly portfolio disclosure for all mutual fund schemes must be done within:
e: AMCs must disclose month-end portfolio (with ISIN) on their website within 10 days of the month-end.

q: A "fundamental attribute" change in a scheme includes:
o: Investment objective, asset allocation pattern, basic structure changes
e: Fundamental attributes: investment objective, asset allocation, risk-return profile, fees structure (load), basic scheme structure. These changes need notice + 30-day exit window.

q: A fund manager change in a scheme must be:
o: Disclosed to all unitholders only at year-end
Communicated through SID/factsheet update; notice via website + email
e: Fund manager changes are material and must be communicated promptly via SID update, factsheet, AMC website, and unitholder communication (email/SMS).

q: The Factsheet of a mutual fund scheme is a:
o: Non-statutory monthly publication providing portfolio + performance snapshot
e: Factsheet is NOT statutory but is a widely-used monthly publication showing portfolio, NAV, AUM, returns, fund manager, ratios — useful for investor decision-making.

q: For an open-ended scheme, in case of fundamental attribute change, the public notice must be given in:
o: One English daily newspaper with nationwide circulation + regional language newspaper at HO
e: Public notice must be given in one English daily nationwide + one regional newspaper at the Mutual Fund's HO location, with at least 30-day no-load exit window.

q: Half-yearly portfolio of all schemes must be disclosed by AMC:
o: On AMC website + sent to unitholders by email
e: Half-yearly portfolios must be disclosed on the AMC website AND e-mailed to all registered unitholders. Physical copies are sent on request.

q: Each scheme NAV must be disclosed by:
e: NAV must be uploaded to AMFI website by 11 PM on the same business day. AMC must also display NAV on its own website.

q: The cover page of the SID must contain:
o: Standard SEBI disclaimer + Riskometer + scheme name + type + AMC details
e: Cover page mandatory contents: SEBI disclaimer (units not approved/recommended by SEBI), Riskometer, scheme name + type, AMC + Trustee contact details, NFO/Reopening dates.

q: An "addendum" to scheme documents is required when:
o: Any change occurs that affects current or prospective investors' decisions
e: Addendum issued for any material change between regular updates — load structure changes, fund manager change, new disclosures, etc. Must accompany KIM until next update.

q: A scheme's "expenses" disclosure in the SID must include:
o: Maximum recurring expenses (TER), load structure, expense slabs
e: SID must disclose maximum TER (with slabs), exit load structure, and any other applicable expenses — so investors know upfront the maximum cost they may bear.

q: The "Performance" section of a scheme's SID must show:
o: 1-year, 3-year, 5-year and since-inception returns + benchmark returns for same periods
e: Past performance disclosure: 1Y/3Y/5Y/since inception alongside benchmark (TRI) for same periods. Forward-looking projections are prohibited.

q: For a Specialized Investment Fund (SIF), instead of the Riskometer, the risk indicator is:
o: Risk-Band with 5 levels (Level 1 lowest, Level 5 highest)
e: SIFs use a Risk-Band with 5 levels — given they're higher-risk than mutual funds. Risk-Band level evaluated monthly.

q: A "fundamental attribute" of a scheme that requires notice + 30-day exit window includes:
o: Investment objective, asset allocation pattern, basic structure
e: Fundamental attributes: investment objective, asset allocation pattern, scheme structure (open/close-ended), fee structure. Changes require notice + 30-day no-load exit.

q: The Riskometer has how many risk levels?
o: 6 (Low, Low to Moderate, Moderate, Moderately High, High, Very High)
e: Riskometer: 6 levels with prescribed colour codes — Low (Irish Green) to Very High (Red).

q: The fundamental attribute change in a scheme requires:
o: Notice + 30-day no-load exit window for unitholders
e: Fundamental attribute change requires written notice (newspaper publication) + 30-day no-load exit window for unitholders to exit if they don't agree.
